identification: Box of Tasmanian art pottery and decorative china. Pieces seen: a brown drip-glaze vase with base signed 'John Campbell Tasmania' (photos 3-5); a second brown/amber drip vase with a chipped rim (photos 6-7, possibly the H. McHugh piece); a base signed 'H McHugh Tasmania H2' (photo 8, a McHugh vase, probably the brown vase with the chipped rim); a navy blue hourglass vase (photos 9-10, base not marked in photos, same style as Campbell/McHugh waisted shapes); a blue/cream drip ribbed vase with frilled rim and chipped lip, base signed with illegible signature and '28' (photos 11-13); also a green fan-tail bird vase/posy, a boxed glass decanter in wooden case, an Usher's Scotch Whisky advertising tray, a tin tray, a Capodimonte-style group of three children with a tortoise, two small floral jugs, a floral milk jug, a two-tier Limoges-style cake stand. Description says John Campbell, others, as is.

viewing_check: Estimate 40-60, current bid $20. Premium is 22%. The prize is the John Campbell (Launceston, 1930s) drip glaze vase; Terapeak shows undamaged Campbell vases at A$36-60 for common shapes up to A$153 for rare marbled glaze (typical A$50), and McHugh vases A$57-115 (typical A$85) in the last 3 years, rising slightly. Auction houses report higher (Carter's median A$180, Gibsons A$700 for three). Chips and damage cut prices hard (A$9 for damaged Campbell). Check the rims for chips (photos 6-7 and 12 show chips), and confirm which vase carries the McHugh base. The Usher's tray sold A$54 once (2024). Postage for ceramics is bulky; Terapeak shows A$14 postage.
